The actual task scope of railroad brake, signal, and switch operators depends on the employer, the yard, and the operating procedures; the same Chinese title may correspond to completely different duties and authority at different organizations.

If you are willing to combine train signals with switching safety and judge according to procedures whether a train can move, this job is worth learning more about. When judging a position, ask three things first: whether you can independently complete brake tests and switch operation, who can approve departure and release, and to whom you escalate when a signal or car anomaly occurs.

The work surfaces of railroad brake, signal, and switch operators are often handled by the same person, but their nature differs: some throw switches to change routes according to instructions, some conduct brake tests and connect cars, and some monitor gauges and signals beside the locomotive. Only by separating them can you judge which kind of ability the position actually requires.

entries: Signals and confirmation｜Observing and relaying train signals｜Observe train signals along the route and verify their meaning for the locomotive engineer, give start or stop signals with signal lights, hand signals, or radio, and observe other crew members' signals to coordinate the work.

Switches and routes｜Throwing switches to change routes｜Push and pull switches to divert cars and receive instructions from the yardmaster or yard conductor about track assignments and cars to be switched.

Braking and tests｜Conducting brake tests and operating hand brakes｜Conduct brake tests to determine the condition of the train's brakes and climb ladders to the top of cars to turn handwheels and set brakes to control speed or park cars.
Car connection｜Connecting and separating cars｜Raise levers to connect and separate cars to make up or break up trains, connect air hoses with wrenches, and inspect couplers, hoses, and journal boxes.

Inspection and maintenance｜Inspecting cars and equipment｜Inspect track, car, and locomotive defects and determine repair needs, sending them for repair when necessary; use hand tools to make minor repairs to couplers, hoses, and journal boxes.

Monitoring and records｜Monitoring gauges and recording｜Monitor locomotive oil levels, temperature, and pressure gauges, check fuel, water, and sand supplies, and record the number of available cars, cars sent for repair, and the type of service.

An oncoming train cannot be warned in time, enlarging the consequences of an accident.

subject.name: Railroad brake, signal, and switch operators
subject.summary:
Railroad brake, signal, and switch operators operate or monitor railroad switches and locomotive gauges and may connect or separate cars to make up or break up trains: they observe and relay train signals; throw switches to divert cars; conduct brake tests and climb ladders to set hand brakes; connect or separate cars and connect air hoses; inspect couplers, hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes; monitor locomotive oil levels, temperature, and pressure gauges; inspect track and car defects and send them for repair; and record available cars and cars sent for repair. This page uses the United States
O*NET exact occupation Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators and Locomotive Firers (53-4022.00); no verifiable exact occupational wage was obtained for the China section, and the insufficient-evidence marker is retained.
